claims.text: The starting material is an as-sintered polycrystalline HfZrTiTa0.53 refractory high-entropy alloy.
The baseline alloy has a quasi-static yield strength of 786 MPa.
The baseline alloy has a quasi-static compressive strength of 1314 MPa.
The baseline alloy has a quasi-static fracture strain of 13.5%.
The baseline alloy undergoes rapid failure and strain localization under dynamic loading.
The proposed intervention is addition of 0.5–1 vol% nanoscale Y2O3 through mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintering.
The processing route will produce uniformly distributed nanoscale oxide dispersoids within the HfZrTiTa0.53 matrix.
The oxide dispersoids will impede dislocation motion.
The oxide dispersoids will promote dislocation accumulation and storage.
Dislocation accumulation around the dispersoids will increase strain-hardening capacity.
The oxide dispersoids will stabilize the microstructure against dynamic recrystallization.
Microstructural stabilization by the oxide dispersoids will inhibit adiabatic shear banding and delay catastrophic failure.
The modified alloy will have 10–20% higher dynamic yield and compressive strength than the baseline.
The modified alloy will increase deformation before fracture or localization by 2–5 percentage points of strain.
The modified alloy will delay the onset of strain localization and adiabatic shear banding.
The modified alloy will exhibit reduced impact-induced energy release and less catastrophic failure.
The predicted improvements apply under adiabatic dynamic compression or impact loading at strain rates from 10^2 to 10^4 s^-1.
Oxide fractions above 2 vol% may cause embrittlement or loss of ductility.
The estimated improvement is based on analogous refractory-HEA and oxide-dispersion-strengthened literature.
